summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old female was admitted after transfer from a psychiatric facility due to altered mental status and lethargy. She had been heavily medicated, leading to toxic encephalopathy. Initial evaluation showed mydriasis and confusion, but imaging and labs were unremarkable. Medication polypharmacy was identified as the cause, and her regimen was simplified to lamotrigine and clonazepam. Her mental clarity improved significantly. She experienced a migraine during admission, treated with Fiorinal, and transient diarrhea that resolved spontaneously. MRSA and C. difficile screens were negative. She was medically cleared and discharged to extended psychiatric care with a streamlined medication plan, including lamotrigine, clonazepam, verapamil, and as-needed analgesics. Her mood and cognition stabilized, and she demonstrated insight into her condition.
